candidate.answerReason: Every group of three starters is determined uniquely by the one player left out, giving four choices.

methods.label: Choose who does not start
methods.explanation:
Choosing three starters from four players leaves exactly one player out. That player can be Lance, Sally, Joy, or Fred, giving four choices.

Every group of three leaves out exactly one person, and different omitted players give different groups. Thus all starter groups are counted exactly once, for \(\boxed{4}\) ways, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Counting the omitted player requires only elementary selection reasoning, with no combination formula.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task concerns an unordered selection of players. The written method counts through a one-to-one correspondence between starter groups and omitted players. The combination-number formula is not needed.

review.mathematicalCheck: Every three-player starter group corresponds uniquely to its one omitted player. The four possible omitted players therefore give exactly four groups.
review.levelCheck: The elementary correspondence is fully explained and appropriate for AMC 8.
review.methodDistinctness: One method is sufficient; a combination-formula alternative adds little.
review.annotationCheck: The unordered-selection target, bijective-counting method, and combination-concept support match the explanation without requiring factorial formulas.
